answer.rationale: Rollback is excluded (compliance-mandated security patch), circuit breakers target dependency outages (not implicated here), and read-replica routing won't help a write-path latency problem. The degradation is confined to the primary region, which matches memory_b2's regional failover pattern. Failover during peak settlement traffic carries real risk to in-flight writes, so it must be executed with write-drain/replication-lag checks rather than a hard cutover; add_capacity (memory_b3) is the fallback if verification shows failover risk to writes is too high. Confidence is moderate because failover at write peak has not been validated in the inherited record under these exact conditions.
